name: Ville de Paris
body: One-year HSTS, nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy, a gzipped sitemap, and Core Web Vitals that pass for real visitors. But the home page has no JSON-LD naming the Ville de Paris or linking its profiles.
lesson: Add a GovernmentOrganization block with name, url, logo, and sameAs. AI answers use it to describe you.
summary: www.paris.fr scores 84 out of 100 (B). 0 checks fail now, 20 are at risk, and 18 pass. Fix first: 5 pages ask search engines not to index it.

fix.title: 5 pages ask search engines not to index it
fix.evidence: /recherche (noindex, nofollow), /recherche/infos (noindex, nofollow), /recherche/lieux (noindex, nofollow), /recherche/sorties (noindex, nofollow) and 1 more.
fix.fix: Remove noindex from pages that should be found, and keep it only on private or duplicate pages.

fix.title: 8 images have no alt attribute
fix.fix: Describe informative images. Give decorative ones alt="".

fix.title: Permissions-Policy is not sent
fix.evidence: Embedded content can ask for the camera, microphone, or location. Missing on all 20 pages analyzed.

fix.title: Tracking tags load with no consent tool in the page
fix.evidence: Matomo appears in the HTML and no consent platform or Google Consent Mode default was found. In the EU, the UK, Brazil, and Colombia this is a legal exposure.
fix.fix: Add a consent platform and set Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied before any tag loads.

fix.title: 35 images have no width or height
fix.evidence: The layout jumps when they load, which hurts Cumulative Layout Shift.
fix.fix: Set width and height (or aspect-ratio) on images.

fix.title: Share cards are missing og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url, twitter:card
fix.evidence: LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Slack, and X build the preview from these tags. The preview in this report shows what they would show today.
fix.fix: Add the missing Open Graph and Twitter tags to every page template.

works.title: Every internal link that was opened answered
AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
Plain http redirects permanently to https
The start page declares its language
Core Web Vitals pass for real visitors
A sitemap answers with valid URLs
